name: com.amircollider.unitydirecttmp
description:
Hand TextMeshPro the font file itself — and every language just works. In your game AND in the Unity Editor.

Since 1.3.0 it does that for a WHOLE PROJECT with no component on anything: Unity DirectTMP ▸ Global Font… asks for a .ttf, and every TextMeshPro label in the project is drawn from it — in the Editor, in Play mode and in the build. Nothing is written into any scene, so a scene reload cannot lose it.

• Global Font — one .ttf, every label, no component, survives domain and scene reloads.
• Point at a font file, not a font asset — drag a .ttf/.otf onto a Direct Font component when you want one label handled specially.
• Font Catalog — every font in the project and on this machine in one list, each showing its real glyph count and exactly which writing systems it can set.
• Editor Font — restyle Unity's OWN interface. If a GameObject named 敵スポーナー or a folder named فونت‌ها shows up as empty boxes in your Hierarchy, this is the fix. Nothing is written to your Unity install; quitting always restores the default.
• Arabic-script text that reads — Persian, Arabic and Urdu joined, in reading order, and wrapped correctly.
• Ordered fallback chains — the first font that has the glyph wins, per character.
• Load fonts at runtime — from StreamingAssets, persistentDataPath, a downloaded byte[], or the player's own installed fonts.
• Health Check — names the project-level faults that make font tooling silently do nothing (TMP Essential Resources, Include Font Data, baked character sets, missing shaders) and fixes them in one click.
• Trilingual editor UI: English, 日本語, فارسی.

Free and MIT licensed. Requires TextMeshPro (bundled with Unity). No other third-party dependencies.

samples.description: One scene, one font, twelve languages — English, CJK, Persian, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai, Hindi and emoji, all from a single .ttf.
